records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the head of state appoint and pay the bank's board
records.summary: The law governing the Bank of Eritrea puts the choice of everyone who runs the bank in the President's hands. Proclamation 93/1997 of 21 January 1997 says in Article 3 that the bank created by Proclamation 32/1993 continues to exist and is from then on governed by this law. Article 13 gives the President the appointment of the Governor for a five-year term, with the approval of the national legislature, and of the Deputy Governor, and says the Governor's pay is set by the President on the Board's recommendation. Article 8 says the names of all nominated Board members are submitted to the President for appointment, that each Board member other than the Governor and his deputy is paid a fee approved by the President for every meeting attended, and that a director who resigns does so by letter to the President, the resignation taking effect only once the President accepts it. The Board also seats a representative of the Ministry of Finance and the Auditor General. The same law states the other side of this: Article 6 says the bank shall be independent from and not subject to instructions by the Government in performing its functions, determining its budget and setting its procedures, and Article 13 lets the President relieve the Governor only for just cause after consulting the legislature. So the record is about who fills and pays the posts, not about a power to direct the bank's decisions. The proclamation sets no end date for these arrangements.
records.source_title: Bank of Eritrea Proclamation 93/1997 (Gazette of Eritrean Laws, via the Library of Congress)
